verses.text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king and ruled sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, as his father Uzziah had done, except that he stayed out of the LORD's temple. The people still acted corruptly.
Jotham built the Upper Gate of the LORD's house and did extensive work on the wall of Ophel.
He built towns in Judah's hill country and put up fortresses and towers in the forests.

He fought and defeated the king of the Ammonites. That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. They paid him the same amount in the second and third years.
Jotham grew powerful because he lived faithfully before the LORD his God.
The rest of what Jotham did, including all his wars and how he lived, is recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five when he became king and ruled sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham died and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.
